literal: Begging when thinking, heart will melt; concealment when thinking, even that which exists without will be destroyed.
translation: The heart melts in sorrow at the mere thought of begging; but at the thought of someone concealing what they have to refuse a beggar, even one's very being is destroyed.
modern: பிறரிடம் சென்று இரந்து கேட்பதை நினைத்தால் உள்ளம் உருகும்; ஆனால் தன்னிடம் இருப்பதை மறைத்து இல்லை என்று சொல்வதை நினைத்தால் உள்ள உயிரும் இல்லாமல் அழிந்துவிடும்.
explanation: This couplet contrasts the deep sorrow of poverty with the greater moral failure of selfishness. The mere thought of having to beg makes a person's heart melt in shame and despair. However, the thought of someone deliberately concealing their wealth to refuse a beggar is so appalling that it destroys the very core of one's existence. The poet uses the melting of the heart to illustrate the pain of the seeker, and total destruction to condemn the cruelty of the one who withholds.
